samples.summary: The `readOnly` effect-dependency change (re-mounting the editor when write authority is lost) has no test anywhere
samples.evidence: The diff adds `readOnly` to the `useEffect` deps at docs-view.tsx:581 with a comment claiming it is the only place the permission is applied to a mounted editor (a session downgraded from `editor` to `viewer` otherwise keeps a fully writable editor). I grepped `packages/frontend/tests/app/docs` for `DocsView`/`docs-view` and for `readOnly`: the only hits are `docs-context-menu.test.tsx`, `docs-table-context-menu.test.tsx` and `docs-find-bar-read-only.test.tsx`, all of which render `DocsContextMenu`/find-bar wrappers with a stubbed `EditorAPI`, never `DocsView` itself. No test rerenders `DocsView` with `readOnly` flipping and asserts a new (read-only) editor is built. Deleting `readOnly` from the deps array again would leave the whole suite green while silently restoring a writable editor for a demoted viewer — a permission guard with zero coverage.
searchedFor: read docs-context-menu.test.tsx wrapper (renders DocsContextMenu, not DocsView)

samples.summary: `requestLayoutRefresh`'s dirty-set preservation (the incremental-layout guarantee for batched edits) is untested
samples.evidence: editor.ts:2545-2549 introduces a layout-only pass that saves `dirtyBlockIds`, runs `recomputeLayout()` (which clears it), then restores `dirty ?? new Set()`. The whole comment is about avoiding a FULL document re-measure on every batched keystroke, and about the `undefined -> empty Set` distinction. Grepping `requestLayoutRefresh` across packages/docs and packages/frontend returns only src hits (text-editor.ts:233/739/3826, editor.ts:2530/2545) — no test file references it. The nearby existing tests (`cursor-move-no-relayout.test.ts`, `incremental-layout.test.ts`, `char-offsets-cache.test.ts`) count re-measures for other paths, so the technique exists in-repo but was not applied here. If the restore line is dropped or changed to `undefined`, nothing turns red; the cost is a full re-layout per keystroke on large documents (visible typing lag), not data loss.
searchedFor: Grep requestLayoutRefresh|dirtyBlockIds across packages/docs and packages/frontend

samples.summary: The newly added `this.readOnly` re-check in the async plain-text paste has no test (and cannot be exercised, since `readOnly` is only ever set in the constructor)
samples.evidence: The diff adds `if (this.disposed || this.pasting || this.readOnly) return;` at text-editor.ts:4261 with a long comment justifying the `readOnly` term specifically ('the permission this session is allowed to exercise is the one that decides'). The two new tests in `large-paste-indicator.test.ts` (lines ~400 and ~440) cover `pasting` and `disposed` only. Grepping `readOnly` in text-editor.ts shows it is assigned once, at line 719 in the constructor, with no setter, so no test could observe this term flipping after the keydown — the added clause is coverage-free and, given the immutable field, unobservable. Failure mode is contained (the outer keydown gate at line 1096 already refuses Cmd+Shift+V in read-only), which is why this is minor rather than major.
searchedFor: Grep readOnly in packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts (only constructor assignment at 719)

samples.summary: `withUndoUnit`'s throw path — depth unwinding and the promised render replay 'including after a throw' — is not tested
samples.evidence: `withUndoUnit` (text-editor.ts ~3839-3850) documents that held renders are replayed 'once — at most once — after the outermost unit commits, including after a throw'. I found no test that makes a unit body throw: grepping the docs test tree for `withUndoUnit` returns nothing, and the new frontend tests in `editor-undo-selection.test.ts` only cover successful units (paint count 1, undo-stack depth +1). If the `finally` were ever narrowed, `undoUnitDepth` would stay >0 and EVERY subsequent `requestRender()` would be swallowed for the life of the editor — a frozen screen — with no test catching it. Grading minor because the current code does use `finally` and the failure would be immediately obvious in manual use.
searchedFor: Grep withUndoUnit across packages/docs/test and packages/frontend/tests

samples.summary: The table-cell Enter branch newly wrapped in `withUndoUnit` has no one-unit test; only the top-level Enter branch is covered
samples.evidence: The diff wraps two distinct Enter paths: the in-cell branch (text-editor.ts ~2651, `enterCellInfo` truthy) and the top-level branch. The new frontend test 'enter over a select-all is one undo unit' selects across top-level paragraphs, so it exercises only the second branch; I found no test placing the caret/selection inside a table cell and asserting a single undo entry. The in-cell branch also calls `invalidateLayout()` inside the unit, which interacts with the new `requestLayoutRefresh` restore-to-`undefined` behaviour, so it is the more delicate of the two.
searchedFor: Grep for cell/table Enter undo tests in packages/docs/test/view

samples.summary: `watchBatches().writesOutsideABatch()` only instruments 9 of the store's write methods, so escaped writes through other mutators would be invisible
samples.evidence: The `writeNames` list in the new `watchBatches()` helper covers insertText/deleteText/deleteBlock/deleteBlockByIndex/mergeBlock/updateBlock/splitBlock/insertBlock/insertBlockAfter. Writes the same actions can perform — `applyStyle`, `setBlockType`, `insertBlocksAfter`, `applyBlockStyle`, `insertImageInline` — are not patched, so a regression that moves one of those outside the unit would still report `writesOutsideABatch() === 0`. The paired `outermost() === 1` assertion limits the damage, hence nit.
searchedFor: compared against write methods listed in packages/docs/src/store/memory.ts

verdict.reason: The cited code is real: docs-view.tsx:572-581 adds `readOnly` to the editor-construction effect's deps with a comment declaring it "the only place that permission is applied" to a mounted editor. I could not find any test that exercises it, and I searched well beyond the reviewer's paths: repo-wide grep of all *.test/*.spec files for `DocsView|docs-view` returns only prose comments (packages/docs/test/view/editor-read-only.test.ts:871, copy-integrity.test.ts:560, frontend yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:598) and unrelated script tests — no test imports docs-view; repo-wide grep of test imports from `@/app/docs/*` yields find-bar, context menus, formatting toolbar, page-setup dialog, link popover, export button, yorkie-doc-store, text-actions and comments helpers, never docs-view; colocated tests under src/app/docs contain only image-insert.test.ts and there is no __tests__ dir there; no e2e/playwright/cypress suite exists anywhere in the repo; no test reads docs-view.tsx as source text and none mentions exhaustive-deps. The nearest indirect coverage, packages/docs/test/view/editor-read-only.test.ts (the only other place `readOnlyDocStore` is referenced besides docs-view.tsx and packages/docs/src), constructs editors directly with a readOnly flag and asserts write neutralization; it never drives docs-view's mount/remount lifecycle, so removing `readOnly` from the deps array would leave it green. Under the test-adequacy rubric this is a changed guard behavior (a demoted viewer keeping a writable editor) with no meaningful test, i.e. a blocking gap in this lane.
